fullBio:
Laura is a Licensed Associate Professional Counselor (APC010070) who received her undergraduate degree from Emory University and her master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Agnes Scott College. Laura's lived experience and personal therapeutic journey inspired her to pursue an encore career as a therapist, with the hope of assisting others in tapping into their potential for healing, growth, and wholeness.

Laura understands that no one knows you better than you, and that making time for reflection and self-exploration can be a powerful and restorative experience. Drawing on your innate strengths and resilience, Laura will meet you where you are with curiosity, presence, and non-judgment as you explore the places you may feel stuck — in old stories, outgrown patterns, and self-limiting ways of being.

Her hope is that your work together will help you connect with deeper meaning, purpose, and your truest sense of self, allowing you to become more present and engaged in your life.
therapeuticApproaches: Existential-Humanistic, Person Centered, Jungian Depth Psychology, Psychodynamic, Transpersonal, Internal Family Systems. Laura uses an integrative approach, tailored to your specific needs, drawing on your innate strengths and resilience.

shortBio: Liz Webb is a Licensed Associate Professional Counselor (LAPC) and National Certified Counselor (NCC). She is a graduate of Mercer University and Samford University, bringing a strong foundation in clinical mental health counseling.
fullBio:
Liz Webb is a Licensed Associate Professional Counselor (LAPC) and National Certified Counselor (NCC). She is a graduate of Mercer University and Samford University, bringing a strong foundation in clinical mental health counseling.

I believe in creating a safe and supportive space where you can be open about whatever you're experiencing in the moment. My goal is to meet you with empathy, compassion, and validation. Together, we can explore your pain, work through challenges, set meaningful goals, and create a plan to help you reach them. Whether you're seeking understanding, growth, healing, or rediscovery, I'm here to walk alongside you on your journey.

I value individuality and want to help you embrace your authentic self — however you show up, wherever you are, and wherever you're going. In our sessions, there are no expectations for who you're "supposed to be." This is your space to express all parts of your experience — the challenges, the joys, the frustrations, the triumphs, and everything in between. My hope is that you cultivate a life that feels genuine, balanced, and fulfilling — one where you can be as authentically you as you feel safe to be.

I practice primarily from a Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) framework, which allows for openness and shared human experience when it benefits your healing process. I also integrate techniques from Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Existential Therapy, Person-Centered Therapy, Internal Family Systems (IFS), and Schema Therapy, tailoring each session to your unique needs.

I work with youth (ages 11–17), adults, and families, and I have experience in PHP, IOP, and outpatient treatment settings.

"May the love and light you bring into the world return to you multiplied." — With peace and compassion, Liz
therapeuticApproaches: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Existential Therapy, Person-Centered Therapy, Internal Family Systems (IFS), Schema Therapy. I tailor these evidence-based approaches to your unique needs and healing journey.

fullBio:
Jackie Malone is an LAPC supervised by Susan Keenan (Georgia / LPC003161). She has a Master in Clinical Rehabilitation Counseling from Georgia State University and a Bachelors degree in Music from The University of Georgia in Piano Performance.

As a former piano teacher and lifelong musician, Jackie believes in the discipline of applying oneself, and that strategic relationships and creativity can be transformative. Her personal journey has informed her decision to become a counselor, and she is uniquely positioned with both experience and tutelage to accompany families, couples and individuals on their paths to recovery.

Jackie is attuned to the needs of those struggling with anxiety, depression, substance use, eating disorders, adjustment disorders, attention deficit disorder, and marginalized communities including LGBTQ+ populations. Her therapeutic orientation is centered in Narrative and Relational Cultural Theory, viewing clients as members of political, cultural, and family systems and stories.
therapeuticApproaches: Compassion Focused, Culturally Sensitive, Dialectical Behavior (DBT), Feminist, Motivational Interviewing, Multicultural, Narrative, Person-Centered, Rational Emotive Behavior (REBT). Her therapeutic orientation is centered in Narrative and Relational Cultural Theory. She looks at clients as members of political, cultural, and family systems and stories. Sometimes these stories build esteem, sometimes they can harm it. She believes understanding these systems and stories assists in finding freedom from and in them.

shortBio: Dr. Alex Crenshaw provides assessment and therapy to adults and couples with a variety of concerns, with a particular emphasis on anxiety and related disorders, trauma, and intimate relationship difficulties. He received his PhD in clinical psychology from the University of Utah in 2020 following completion of his predoctoral internship at the Charleston Consortium. fullBio:
Dr. Alex Crenshaw provides assessment and therapy to adults and couples with a variety of concerns, with a particular emphasis on anxiety and related disorders, trauma, and intimate relationship difficulties. He received his PhD in clinical psychology from the University of Utah in 2020 following completion of his predoctoral internship at the Charleston Consortium. He subsequently completed a postdoctoral fellowship at Toronto Metropolitan University from 2020-2023.

He aims to develop a strong working relationship and to fit treatment to the values and goals of the client. He enjoys working with adults and couples from a variety of backgrounds, races/ethnicities, sexual orientations, and gender identities.

In addition to his time at Peachtree Psychology, Dr. Crenshaw is an Assistant Professor of Psychology at Kennesaw State University, where he teaches a variety of courses and conducts research. His research focuses on the role of empathy and conflict patterns in intimate relationships, treatments for intimate relationship problems and PTSD, and improving how we scientifically test psychological interventions. He is a member of the Association for Behavioral and Cognitive Therapies, Society for a Science of Clinical Psychology, and Society for the Improvement of Psychological Science.
therapeuticApproaches: Dr. Crenshaw's approach emphasizes evidence-based practice, integrating the best available research evidence with each client's unique preferences, history, and past therapy experiences. He has extensive training in evidence-based cognitive behavioral treatments, including Standard Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and Integrative Behavioral Couple Therapy for intimate relationship difficulties. He also has specialty training in several evidence-based therapies for PTSD, including Prolonged Exposure, Cognitive Processing Therapy, and Cognitive Behavioral Conjoint Therapy.

fullBio:
Dr. Jeannine Jannot holds a doctorate in developmental psychology and brings over 25 years of experience working with students, parents, and adults. Her deep understanding of how the brain develops and learns makes her uniquely qualified to help individuals of all ages build the skills they need to thrive academically and professionally.

As a student coach, Jeannine works with tweens, teens, and college students who struggle with executive functioning — the underlying skills that drive academic success. She helps students develop personalized strategies for organization, time management, planning, and self-advocacy, empowering them to take ownership of their learning.

Jeannine also coaches adults seeking to improve their productivity and manage the competing demands of professional and personal life. Whether it's ADHD-related challenges or simply the overwhelm of modern life, she provides practical, research-backed strategies that create lasting change.

therapeuticApproaches: Sarah's relational style integrates ACT, DBT, CBT, ERP, MBSR (Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction), ASIST (Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training) Suicide to Hope, and neuroscience/polyvagal theory. fullBio:
Erin Benator is a Clinical Mental Health Intern obtaining her Master's degree in Mental Health Counseling from Wake Forest University. She also holds a BFA in Writing from the Savannah College of Art and Design and an MA in Museum Studies from Marist College - Lorenzo de' Medici Institute.

Erin specializes in helping neurodivergent teens and adults successfully navigate life transitions. Her lived experience informed her desire to be a counselor, providing her with knowledge and skills to support this unique population. She has a background as a personal trainer, which informs her holistic view of health and wellness as rooted in both psychological and physiological self-care.

Erin's mission is to help teens and adults overcome self-doubt and perfectionist tendencies and embrace their authentic selves. She supports her clients in replacing feelings of never being "enough", not belonging, guilt, and shame by providing them with functional tools to increase emotional regulation, self-esteem, and social connection. Her therapeutic approach is grounded in Internal Family Systems (IFS), viewing healing as a process of recognizing and integrating all parts of oneself.
therapeuticApproaches: Internal Family Systems (IFS). Erin views individuals as a system composed of wounded and protected "inner parts" guided by one's foundational "Self". By accessing these inner parts, one can recognize and heal them, becoming more internally and externally connected. She also stresses the importance of mind-body connection in her practice, viewing health and wellness as rooted in psychological and physiological self-care.

fullBio:

Lynn holds a Master of Social Work from Smith College for Social Work in Northampton, MA, and a Master of Divinity (MDiv) from Vanderbilt Divinity School in Nashville, Tennessee. Her work focuses on helping clients find resources for strength and capacity to cope with changes as they age, often through making meaning out of their losses and life transitions.

Her therapeutic philosophy emphasizes respect for the client and mutually agreed upon goals, helping clients find their way for coping with life's challenges. A non-judgmental presence through the therapeutic process allows clients to explore their physical, emotional, and spiritual thoughts and beliefs to find healing and hope.
therapeuticApproaches: Lynn believes that respect for the client and mutually agreed upon goals help clients find their way for coping with life's challenges in all of life's transitions. A non-judgmental presence through the therapeutic process allows clients to explore their physical, emotional, and spiritual thoughts and beliefs to find healing and hope. She emphasizes making meaning out of losses to make peace with life's inevitable transitions.

shortBio: Amanda Gaines is a Master Social Worker with a Bachelor of Science in Biology from Wingate University and a Master of Social Work from Kennesaw State University, where she served as Vice President of the Phi Alpha Social Work Honor Society.
fullBio:
Amanda Gaines is a Master Social Worker with a Bachelor of Science in Biology from Wingate University and a Master of Social Work from Kennesaw State University, where she served as Vice President of the Phi Alpha Social Work Honor Society.

In her practice, Amanda takes an inclusive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approach. She believes that each client's story is unique, and she tailors each session to meet the individual needs of the person in front of her. Amanda understands that meaningful change in therapy takes patience, dedication, and courage—and she is passionate about walking alongside her clients as they navigate their own journeys of growth and healing.

Amanda has worked in organizations including The Department of Veterans Affairs, immigration nonprofits, and virtual intensive outpatient programs (IOPs). She has experience collaborating with clients across the lifespan, from young adults (18+) through older adults (65+), and has a particular passion for supporting young adults and members of the LGBTQIA+ community. Her focus is on creating an empowering, affirming space where clients feel seen, supported, and encouraged to thrive.
therapeuticApproaches: My approach is grounded in warmth, collaboration, and respect for each person's unique journey. I work from a person-centered foundation, creating a safe and nonjudgmental space where you can explore your experiences openly and at your own pace. Drawing from Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and Solution-Focused strategies, I help clients build practical skills while deepening insight and self-understanding. Together, we focus on strengthening your ability to stay present, manage difficult emotions, and move toward the values that matter most to you. In our work, we highlight your strengths, identify what's already working, and develop meaningful steps that support healing and growth. My goal is to help you feel empowered, understood, and supported as you navigate challenges and create lasting change.
